src.l: Saltzmann, Johann Rudolph, 1622, Saltzmann, Johann Rudolph: Anaskeuē hopliatrias
src.q: No less pleasant and worthy of investigation is that most vexing question of the natural philosophers: > Whether the unguentum armarium [weapon salve], which is smeared only onto a cloth or a bloody sword and neatly applied to the wounds of a patient, whether they are present or many miles away, brings about a cure naturally.

s: Kircher, Athanasius, Athanasii Kircheri Societatis Jesu Magnes sive de arte magnetica opus tripartium quo universa magnetis natura, eiusque in omnibus scientiis & artibus usus, nova medthodo explicatur, ac praeterae e viribus & prodigiosis effectibus magneticarum, aliarumque abditarum naturae motionum in elementis, lapidibus, plantis, animalibus, elucescentium, multa hucusque incognita natureae arcana, per physica, medica, chymica, & mathematica omnis generis experimenta recluduntur (1654), on weapon salve and powder of sympathy: Kircher on why it is called magnetic and armary: applied to weapons to heal at a distance.

src.l: Kircher, Athanasius, 1654, Athanasii Kircheri Societatis Jesu Magnes sive de arte magnetica opus tripartium quo universa magnetis natura, eiusque in omnibus scientiis & artibus usus, nova medthodo explicatur, ac praeterae e viribus & prodigiosis effectibus magneticarum, aliarumque abditarum naturae motionum in elementis, lapidibus, plantis, animalibus, elucescentium, multa hucusque incognita natureae arcana, per physica, medica, chymica, & mathematica omnis generis experimenta recluduntur
src.q: On the Microcosmic Magnet, or the Hoplochrysma [Weapon-salve], or the Unguentum Armarium [Armary Ointment]. Not long ago, there emerged from the Stygian workshop, I think, a certain ointment which, from the action by which it is falsely believed to heal the wounded at a distance, is called Magnetic;

s: Fludd, Robert, Mosaic Philosophy (1638), on weapon salve and powder of sympathy: Fludd answering Foster, who attributed the salve's power to the Devil.

src.l: Fludd, Robert, 1638, Mosaic Philosophy
src.q: were saying, "Although Demetrius the Ephesian with his followers attributed all power to the fictitious goddess Diana, and Foster [attributes] the secret and wonderful power of healing through the Unguentum armarium [Weapon Salve] to the Devil, as the Prince of this world, without any consideration of this text: yet it is certain that there is God the Father, from whom are all things, and consequently this act in healing (and through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are

s: Foster, William, Hoplocrisma-spongus: or, a sponge to wipe away the weapon-salve (1631), on weapon salve and powder of sympathy: Foster 1631: the armary ointment now wanders through villages and cities.

src.l: Foster, William, 1631, Hoplocrisma-spongus: or, a sponge to wipe away the weapon-salve
src.q: This Armary Ointment [another name for the Weapon-Salve; original: "Unguentum Armarium"], which a few years ago was known to almost no one by name, now wanders everywhere through many villages and cities of this kingdom to the contempt of God and legitimate art.

s: Robert Fludd, Das höchste Gut (Summum Bonum) (1621), on natural magic: Ficino (Apologia, as quoted by Fludd): natural magic seeks heavenly benefits for the body by natural means.

src.l: Robert Fludd, 1621, Das höchste Gut (Summum Bonum)
src.q: rather, I have considered natural magic (Magia naturalis), which seeks to obtain the benefits of heavenly means for physical well-being through natural methods.

s: Hildebrand, Wolfgang, Hildebrand, Wolfgang: Wolffgangi Hildebrands new augirte, weitverbesserte und vielvermehrte Magia Naturalis: Das ist Künst und Wünderbüch. 1. (1650). - 50 Bl. : Ill. (1650), on natural magic: Hildebrand: performing wonders with the aid of natural things.

src.l: Hildebrand, Wolfgang, 1650, Hildebrand, Wolfgang: Wolffgangi Hildebrands new augirte, weitverbesserte und vielvermehrte Magia Naturalis: Das ist Künst und Wünderbüch. 1. (1650). - 50 Bl. : Ill.
src.q: Wolfgangi Hildebrandi MAGIA NATURALIS Magia Naturalis That is: A highly useful and proven Book of Arts , therein are contained many magnificent and secret arts , namely how one may perform all manner of miracles with the aid of natural things , which have never before been seen nor heard .

s: Roth-Scholtz, Friedrich (1687-1736), Deutsches theatrum chemicum, auf welchem der berühmtesten Philosophen und Alchymisten Schrifften, die von dem Stein der Weisen, von Verwandlung der schlechten Metalle in bessere ... handeln ... vorgestellet werden / Erster Theil. (1728), on natural magic: Roth-Scholtz: hidden virtues of lower things joined to the stars by natural magic.

src.l: Roth-Scholtz, Friedrich (1687-1736), 1728, Deutsches theatrum chemicum, auf welchem der berühmtesten Philosophen und Alchymisten Schrifften, die von dem Stein der Weisen, von Verwandlung der schlechten Metalle in bessere ... handeln ... vorgestellet werden / Erster Theil.
src.q: Through its rays, the secrets of all celestial stars and the hidden things of lower matters are to be known, and their virtues joined in an artificial marriage, which Natural Magic [original: "Magia Naturalis"] extends even to angelic intelligence.

s: Oetinger, Friedrich Christoph, Die Philosophie der Alten wiederkommend in der güldenen Zeit : worinnen von den unsichtbaren Anfängen des spiritus rectoris oder bildenden Geists in den Pflanzen ... gehandelt wird (1762), on natural magic: Oetinger: natural magic as a lost science surviving among Black Forest farmers.

src.l: Oetinger, Friedrich Christoph, 1762, Die Philosophie der Alten wiederkommend in der güldenen Zeit : worinnen von den unsichtbaren Anfängen des spiritus rectoris oder bildenden Geists in den Pflanzen ... gehandelt wird
src.q: Magia Naturalis [natural magic] is to be counted among the lost sciences. There are still remnants among farmers in the Black Forest, even if the mechanists laugh about it.

s: Anonymous, Treatise on Talismans and Astral Figures: Demonstrating Their Natural Effects and Virtuous Use (1658), on talismans: the theory: the image formed determines that the influence communicates itself to the talisman.

src.l: Anonymous, 1658, Treatise on Talismans and Astral Figures: Demonstrating Their Natural Effects and Virtuous Use
src.q: 74 THE TALISMANS sign of his operation; inasmuch as by thus forming for himself the image of the quality he intends to introduce into the Talisman, this image determines, by the same law, that this influence shall communicate itself particularly to the Talisman, and it is precisely and

s: Maslama al-Majriti, The Goal of the Wise (Ghayat al-Hakim) (960), on talismans: Picatrix: making the talisman's members must follow nature.

src.l: Maslama al-Majriti, 960, The Goal of the Wise (Ghayat al-Hakim)
src.q: for scorpions flee from that talisman. The crafting of these members is a type of approximation, but the original work must be according to the reality of nature.

s: Thomas Patrick Hughes, A Dictionary of Islam (1885), on talismans: the word: Arabic tilsam, plural talasim.

src.l: Thomas Patrick Hughes, 1885, A Dictionary of Islam
src.q: An inquirer. A term generally used for a student of divinity, is Ṭālibu ’l-‘ilm. TALISMAN. Arabic (طلسم) ṭilsam; pl. ṭalāsim. The English word is a corruption of the Arabic.

s: Papus (Gérard Encausse), Elementary Treatise on Practical Magic (1893), on talismans: Papus: talismans as figures of the creative forms of the astral.

src.l: Papus (Gérard Encausse), 1893, Elementary Treatise on Practical Magic
src.q: REALIZATION Talismans. We have previously indicated the theory of talismans, considered as the exact figures of the creative forms of the astral.

s: Silvestro Mazzolini (Prierias), Three Books on the Miraculous Things of Witches, Demons (1521), on ensouling statues: Hermes: as God made the celestial gods, man makes the gods in temples, statues animated.

src.l: Silvestro Mazzolini (Prierias), 1521, Three Books on the Miraculous Things of Witches, Demons
src.q: Augustine recounts that Hermes professes that just as God is the maker of the celestial gods, so man is the maker of the gods who are in temples, content with human proximity—I mean (he says) statues animated by sense and full of spirit, etc.

s: Proclus, Proclus: Commentary on Plato's Timaeus, Vol. III (1906), on ensouling statues: Proclus: the telestic art makes statues share in god and foretell.

src.l: Proclus, 1906, Proclus: Commentary on Plato's Timaeus, Vol. III
src.q: Furthermore, that is also absurd: that the telestic [ritual/initiatory] art, and oracles, and statues of gods are established on the earth, and that things made from partial and perishable matter are made suitable through certain symbols to share in god, to be moved by him, and to foretell the future, while the creator of the wholes has not set divine souls, intellects, and gods over the whole, imperishable, and complete parts of the world?

s: St. Augustine, De Civitate Dei (1467), on ensouling statues: 1467 Augustine's quotation of the Asclepius statues passage.

src.l: St. Augustine, 1467, De Civitate Dei
src.q: Statues animated, full of sense and spirit, doing such great and many things; statues with foreknowledge of the future, predicting things which perhaps every prophet might be ignorant of in many and various matters;

s: Henry Rowlands, Mona Antiqua Restaurata: An Archaeological Discourse on the Antiquities of the Isle of Anglesey (1766), on ensouling statues: Iamblichus's idols filled with divine influence.

src.l: Henry Rowlands, 1766, Mona Antiqua Restaurata: An Archaeological Discourse on the Antiquities of the Isle of Anglesey
src.q: our men-pillars) they accounted Statuas animatas, sensu & spiritu plenas, as Trismegistus calls them; or ’Αγάλματα θείας μετουσίας ἀνάπλεα, as Jamblichus words it. i. e. "Idols filled with divine influence, and animated statues furnished with something within them that hath life and perception."

s: Shankaracharya (attr.), The Essence of the Manifested World Tantra (1935), on installing life in images: tantra: perform the prāṇapratiṣṭhā, placing the life-nature into the vessel with its mantra.

src.l: Shankaracharya (attr.), 1935, The Essence of the Manifested World Tantra

s: Anonymous, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། མ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 17) (1982), on installing life in images: consecration as summoning the syllable Hum to enter and remain firm.

src.l: Anonymous, 1982, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། མ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 17)
src.q: Finally, the consecration [original: rab gnas]. This refers to the act of summoning and causing the syllable Hum to enter and remain firm.

s: Anonymous, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཉ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 9) (1982), on installing life in images: etymology: pratiṣṭhā/rab gnas as 'excellent abiding'.

src.l: Anonymous, 1982, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཉ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 9)
src.q: Regarding the first, the etymological definition: prakashananadi pratishtha means "consecration" [Tibetan: rab gnas] because it is an "excellent abiding.

s: Anonymous, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཉ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 9) (1982), on installing life in images: which paintings, scriptures and statues are fit to be consecrated.

src.l: Anonymous, 1982, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཉ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 9)
src.q: Regarding the paintings of the sublime Dharma, the volumes of scripture, and those statues that are excellent in proportion, or even those of lesser quality, which possess the tantra of perfect bliss: by knowing their specific types and characteristics, it is appropriate to perform the consecration rab gnas [consecration/pratishtha] rituals.

s: Allix, Pierre, Ausspruch der alten Jüdischen Kirchen (1707), on golem: Allix: a clay image given conjurations in its ears walks.

src.l: Allix, Pierre, 1707, Ausspruch der alten Jüdischen Kirchen
src.q: They have another sorcery called Hamor golim [likely a corruption of 'homer,' meaning clay, or referring to a Golem]; they make an image of clay like a human being, whisper or murmur some conjurations into its ears, and the image walks.

s: Allix, Pierre, Ausspruch der alten Jüdischen Kirchen (1707), on golem: Allix: Jews said to form a lump of clay like a human.

src.l: Allix, Pierre, 1707, Ausspruch der alten Jüdischen Kirchen
src.q: To what Brenz brought forward concerning the Hamor golim [clay golem], he answers: The Mumar [apostate] writes that among the Jews there are those who take a lump of clay, form it, and make it like a human being;
src.qo: Auf das / was der Brentz von dem Hamor golim fürgebracht / antwortet er: Der מומר Mumar (Abtrünnige) schreibt/es werden unter denen Juden gefunden / die einen Laim-Kloßen nehmen / formiren und machen ihn einem Menschengleich /

s: Horowitz, Isaiah ben Abraham Halevi, The Two Tablets of the Covenant (1698), on golem: Midrash: Adam as an unformed golem before animation.

src.l: Horowitz, Isaiah ben Abraham Halevi, 1698, The Two Tablets of the Covenant
src.q: As the Midrash Rabbah says on the portion of Ki Tissa: when Adam was still an unformed mass (golem), the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him every righteous person destined to descend from him.

s: Paracelsus; ed. A.E. Waite, Hermetical and Alchemical Writings of Paracelsus (1894), on homunculus: Paracelsus: whether Nature and Art can beget a man without a womb.

src.l: Paracelsus; ed. A.E. Waite, 1894, Hermetical and Alchemical Writings of Paracelsus
src.q: But neither must we by any means forget the generation of homunculi. For there is some truth in this thing, although for a long time it was held in a most occult manner and with secrecy, while there was no little doubt and question among some of the old Philosophers, whether it was possible to Nature and Art, that a man should be begotten without the female body and the natural womb.

s: Daniel Sennert, On the Consensus and Dissensus of Chemists with Aristotelian and Galenic Scholars, Book I (1619), on homunculus: Sennert reports the method of generating a homunculus without parents.

src.l: Daniel Sennert, 1619, On the Consensus and Dissensus of Chemists with Aristotelian and Galenic Scholars, Book I
src.q: On Homunculi. In book 1, On the Generation of Natural Things, he teaches, and also proposes the method by which a homunculus [a tiny, man-made human being] may be generated without father and mother, by the benefit of the Chemical art;

s: Becher, Johann Joachim, Psychosophia oder Seelen-Weissheit (1705), on homunculus: a 1705 dismissal of Paracelsus's homuncio as fable.

src.l: Becher, Johann Joachim, 1705, Psychosophia oder Seelen-Weissheit
src.q: Of almost the same kind of fable is the homuncio [homunculus or little man] of Theophrastus Paracelsus. Not only all sensible heathens, but also all Christians know that no herb has grown to ward off death, and that no one can escape death.

s: Herbert Silberer, Problems of Mysticism and Its Symbolism (1917), on homunculus: the homunculus is to be raised like a child.

src.l: Herbert Silberer, 1917, Problems of Mysticism and Its Symbolism
src.q: We call it homunculus and it should then be brought up just like another child with great diligence and care till it comes to its days of understanding.

s: Giovanni Pontano, Complete Works (Opera Omnia) (1518), on offerings to place spirits: 1470: Alexander Severus performs morning rites in his lararium.

src.l: Giovanni Pontano, 1518, Complete Works (Opera Omnia)
src.q: He performed divine service in his own Lararium [shrine] early in the morning, whenever he had not slept with his wife. In this Lararium, he had statues placed of the best princes, as well as of the most holy men;

s: H.P. Blavatsky, Theosophical Glossary (1906), on offerings to place spirits: what a lararium was: where the Lares were kept.

src.l: H.P. Blavatsky, 1906, Theosophical Glossary
src.q: a mystic term in alchemy, having quite a different meaning from that usually attributed to it. Lararium (Lat.). An apartment in the house of ancient Romans where the Lares or household gods were preserved, with other family relics.

s: Franz Cumont, Texts and Monuments Relating to the Mysteries of Mithra, Vol. 2 (1899), on offerings to place spirits: a lararium found with statues of gods.

src.l: Franz Cumont, 1899, Texts and Monuments Relating to the Mysteries of Mithra, Vol. 2
src.q: In the ruins of a luxurious house from the time of Constantine or slightly earlier, a lararium was found with a statue of Isis-Fortuna and figurines of Serapis, Jupiter, Hecate, Venus, Mars, Hercules, etc.

s: Patañjali (with Vyāsa, Vācaspati Miśra, Bhojadeva), Yoga-Sūtra with Three Classical Commentaries (Sanskrit) (1904), on prāṇāyāma: Yoga Sutra 2.49: regulation of the flow of inhalation and exhalation is pranayama.

src.l: Patañjali (with Vyāsa, Vācaspati Miśra, Bhojadeva), 1904, Yoga-Sūtra with Three Classical Commentaries (Sanskrit)
src.q: || 48 || After the mastery of posture, he speaks of prāṇāyāma [breath control]: 49. When that is accomplished, the regulation of the flow of inhalation and exhalation is prāṇāyāma When steadiness in posture is achieved, the specific limb of yoga known as prāṇāyāma, caused by that steadiness, is to be practiced.

s: Shankaracharya (attr.), The Essence of the Manifested World Tantra (1935), on prāṇāyāma: tantric instruction: exhale through the right nostril, inhale through the left.

src.l: Shankaracharya (attr.), 1935, The Essence of the Manifested World Tantra

s: Svatmarama, Light on the Yoga of Force with Commentaries (1450), on prāṇāyāma: hatha text: once posture is firm, practise breath control as the guru instructs.

src.l: Svatmarama, 1450, Light on the Yoga of Force with Commentaries
src.q: 37 Second Instruction Root Text: Now, when the posture is firm, the yogi—having mastered the senses and consuming wholesome, moderate food—should practice breath control prāṇāyāma according to the path instructed by the guru.

s: Anonymous, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཀ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 2) (1982), on tummo (inner heat): The wisdom-fire of candali blazes in the navel, fanned by the winds.

src.l: Anonymous, 1982, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཀ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 2)
src.q: Now, the internal explanation shall be given: Within the great hearth of the navel lotus, the wisdom-fire of caṇḍālī [the inner heat or tummo] blazes, fanned by the winds of karma.

s: Anonymous, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཆ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 7) (1982), on tummo (inner heat): Tummo stirred at the navel melts the bindu, which descends.

src.l: Anonymous, 1982, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཆ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 7)
src.q: Through experiencing joyful bliss together with her, the tummo [inner heat] is stirred by the downward-clearing wind at the navel. Burned by the light of the straight lines of the fierce fire of tummo, the moon-like bindu [vital essence] descends along with the indrawing wind.

s: Gangtey Monastery Collection, Zhal gdams nor bu'i phra bkod (1700), on tummo (inner heat): Fire arises from the red drop and passes through the central channel.

src.l: Gangtey Monastery Collection, 1700, Zhal gdams nor bu'i phra bkod
src.q: From that red drop of the lotus, which is the tummo [inner heat] by nature, fire arises. It passes through the interior of the father's jewel-vajra, enters the central channel avadhuti, and causes the enlightened mind to descend from the syllable HAM.

s: Anonymous, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ན (Derge Tengyur, vol. 13) (1982), on tummo (inner heat): When the winds stop moving, candali blazes from the navel.

src.l: Anonymous, 1982, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ན (Derge Tengyur, vol. 13)
src.q: Regarding the life-sustaining and downward-clearing winds: here, if the winds do not flow upward or downward, the caṇḍālī [inner heat; tummo] blazes from the navel.

s: Charaka, चरकसंहिता (Caraka Saṃhitā) (1819), on rasāyana: Caraka: those devoted to rasayana lived thousands of years without aging.

src.l: Charaka, 1819, चरकसंहिता (Caraka Saṃhitā)
src.q: Caraka-Saṃhitā [Chapter 1] In the past, those devoted to rasāyana lived for thousands of years without aging, weakness, exhaustion, or death.

s: Nāgārjuna, Rasaratnākara (manuscript) (1891), on rasāyana: Rasaratnakara: rasayana is the cause of long life once mercury is perfected.

src.l: Nāgārjuna, 1891, Rasaratnākara (manuscript)
src.q: This rasayana [alchemy of rejuvenation] is the cause of long life on earth once the mercury is perfected. Take one hundred palas [a traditional unit of weight] of abhaya [the Chebulic Myrobalan fruit] and the same of amalaka [Indian Gooseberry].

s: Vagbhata, अष्टाङ्गहृदय (Aṣṭāṅgahṛdayam) (1891), on rasāyana: Astangahrdaya: apply rasayana after cleansing therapy, at the right time.

src.l: Vagbhata, 1891, अष्टाङ्गहृदय (Aṣṭāṅgahṛdayam)
src.q: The physician who knows the time should apply rasāyana [rejuvenating therapies] after the cleansing therapy. The word "time" is a pointer for place, strength, body type, diet, assimilation, and constitution.

s: Anonymous, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། པེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 182) (1982), on rasāyana: a Buddhist reflection on the limited capacity of rejuvenation therapy.

src.l: Anonymous, 1982, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། པེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 182)
src.q: Even if one comes to possess strength through rasāyana [rejuvenation therapy] and proper application, nevertheless, because the capacity of rejuvenation therapy is strictly limited, strength is undoubtedly limited as well.

s: Mira Roy (ed.), Rasārṇavakalpa (English critical edition) (1976), on kāyakalpa: defines kayakalpa as physical culture to make the body divine.

src.l: Mira Roy (ed.), 1976, Rasārṇavakalpa (English critical edition)

s: Anonymous, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། སྣ་ཚོགས། ནོ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 211) (1982), on chülen (essence extraction): definition: any medicine that prevents white hair and illness is called chülen.

src.l: Anonymous, 1982, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། སྣ་ཚོགས། ནོ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 211)
src.q: Next, the chapter on the Tantra of Medicinal Rejuvenation Rasayana [essence extraction or alchemy] and Virility will be explained. In that regard, any medicine that prevents white hair and illness is called Chülen [taking the essence].

s: Anonymous, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། གསོ་རིག ཨེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 199) (1982), on chülen (essence extraction): chülen increases lifespan and vigor, clarifies the senses.

src.l: Anonymous, 1982, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། གསོ་རིག ཨེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 199)
src.q: In particular, it becomes a supreme chülen [essence extraction or rejuvenation tonic] that clarifies the sensory organs. It increases and expands lifespan and physical vigor, improves the voice, and conquers diseases of the semen and blood.

s: Anonymous, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། གསོ་རིག ཧེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 198) (1982), on chülen (essence extraction): a chulen taken with milk doubles the lifespan.

src.l: Anonymous, 1982, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། གསོ་རིག ཧེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 198)
src.q: This chulen [essence extraction or rejuvenation] medicine taken with a handful of milk, when prepared by smearing in an iron vessel, produces even greater qualities than previously described and doubles the lifespan.

s: Anonymous, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཟི (Derge Tengyur, vol. 53) (1982), on chülen (essence extraction): oral instructions on chulen to protect body and speech.

src.l: Anonymous, 1982, བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཟི (Derge Tengyur, vol. 53)
src.q: After prostrating to the Gurus, I shall explain the oral instructions on Chulen [essence extraction or alchemy] To constantly protect the body and speech.

s: Shen Kuo, Dream Pool Essays (1088), on yangsheng (nourishing life): Shen Kuo: nourishing-life practitioners say guarding the Yellow Court brings longevity.

src.l: Shen Kuo, 1088, Dream Pool Essays
src.q: Therefore, practitioners of nourishing life yangsheng [nourishing life] say: "If one can guard the Yellow Court, one can attain longevity.

s: 巢元方, 巢氏諸病源候總論·卷十五~卷二十一 (vol 4) (598), on yangsheng (nourishing life): Yangsheng fang daoyin exercise instruction (Chao Yuanfang).

src.l: 巢元方, 598, 巢氏諸病源候總論·卷十五~卷二十一 (vol 4)
src.q: Methods of nourishing vitality and daoyin [guiding and pulling exercises] state: Sit upright, extend the waist and chest, and look up, raising the head. Place the fingers of both hands facing each other, pressing firmly forward against the mat so that the body is taut.

s: Ge Hong, Baopuzi: Inner Chapters (1778), on yangsheng (nourishing life): Ge Hong on those who refuse the methods of yangsheng.

src.l: Ge Hong, 1778, Baopuzi: Inner Chapters
src.q: They refuse to seek out methods of yangsheng [nourishing life], choosing instead to whittle it down, torment it, exhaust it, and drain it dry.

s: Li Yu (李漁), 笠翁一家言全集 (Lǐwēng Collected Works), Vol. 24 (1730), on yangsheng (nourishing life): Li Yu puts joy first among the methods of nourishing life.

src.l: Li Yu (李漁), 1730, 笠翁一家言全集 (Lǐwēng Collected Works), Vol. 24
src.q: Here, I discuss the methods of nurturing life yangsheng [nourishing life/health preservation], and I place the pursuit of joy first. To urge people to pursue joy, yet to frighten them with the cycle of life and death, is to follow this very intent.

s: Ge Hong, Baopuzi: Inner Chapters (1778), on daoyin (guiding and pulling): Baopuzi: emulate daoyin to extend years.

src.l: Ge Hong, 1778, Baopuzi: Inner Chapters
src.q: Therefore, the perfected persons zhenren [perfected beings] only instruct us to emulate their daoyin [guiding and pulling gymnastics] to extend years, and imitate their breath consumption to eliminate grain, not to learn their hibernating in the soil or flying through the heavens.
src.qo: 是以真人但令學其道引以延年法其食 氣以絕穀不學其土蟄與天飛也

s: 巢元方, 巢氏諸病源候總論·卷十~卷十四 (vol 3) (598), on daoyin (guiding and pulling): a concrete daoyin instruction from the Yangsheng fang.

src.l: 巢元方, 598, 巢氏諸病源候總論·卷十~卷十四 (vol 3)
src.q: The Prescriptions for Nourishing Life on daoyin [guiding and pulling exercises] state: Sit and straighten the waist. Raise the left hand with the palm facing upward. Draw back the right arm with the right hand facing downward.

s: various (Daoist); incl. 譚峭 Tan Qiao, 道宗六書 :6種, 36卷. [China] : 黄世厚, 明萬曆丙子 [4年, 1576]. (1576), on daoyin (guiding and pulling): Zhuangzi: daoyin practitioners who nurture the form and seek Pengzu's age.

src.l: various (Daoist); incl. 譚峭 Tan Qiao, 1576, 道宗六書 :6種, 36卷. [China] : 黄世厚, 明萬曆丙子 [4年, 1576].
src.q: This is what the scholars of daoyin [guiding and pulling breath], the people who nourish the physical form, and those who seek a lifespan like that of Pengzu, are fond of.
src.qo: 此道引之士，養形之人，彭祖壽考者之所好也。

s: 陶弘景 Tao Hongjing (456–536), Declarations of the Perfected (1782), on daoyin (guiding and pulling): herbs useless without breath circulation and daoyin.

src.l: 陶弘景 Tao Hongjing (456–536), 1782, Declarations of the Perfected
src.q: The Lord said: "If one ingests herbs and botanical medicines but does not understand the arts of the bedchamber, and does not practice circulating the qi [vital energy] and gymnastic exercises daoyin [guiding and pulling exercises], taking medicine yields no benefit, and one will ultimately never attain the Way.

s: Wu Qian (ed.), 御纂醫宗金鑑 (Golden Mirror of Medicine), Vol. 2 (1742), on daoyin (guiding and pulling): daoyin and breathing prevent blockage of the orifices.

src.l: Wu Qian (ed.), 1742, 御纂醫宗金鑑 (Golden Mirror of Medicine), Vol. 2
src.q: Through daoyin [guiding and pulling exercises], tuna [breathing exercises], acupuncture, moxibustion, or herbal massage, one can prevent the blockage of the nine orifices.

s: 葛洪 Ge Hong (284–363), Biographies of Divine Immortals, vol.2 (332), on embryonic breathing: 320: closing and swallowing the breath is called embryonic breathing.

src.l: 葛洪 Ge Hong (284–363), 332, Biographies of Divine Immortals, vol.2
src.q: holding the qi [breath] and swallowing it is called taixi [embryonic breathing]. Rinsing the mouth with the spring beneath the tongue and swallowing it is called taishi [embryonic feeding].

s: Various Taoist Masters, Essence of the Taoist Canon (1922), on embryonic breathing: Lord Lao: humans do not die because of embryonic breathing, like a fetus without nose or mouth.

src.l: Various Taoist Masters, 1922, Essence of the Taoist Canon
src.q: " The Method of Embryonic Breathing Lord Lao said: "The reason humans do not die lies within Embryonic Breathing Taixi (胎息). A deep, subtle form of internal breathing likened to a fetus in the womb, which does not rely on the nose and mouth.

s: 張伯端 Zhang Boduan (987–1082) et al.; ed. 吳勉學 Wu Mianxue, 道言內外秘訣全書 (1573), on embryonic breathing: 1075 warning: forcing the breath in brings illness.

src.l: 張伯端 Zhang Boduan (987–1082) et al.; ed. 吳勉學 Wu Mianxue, 1573, 道言內外秘訣全書
src.q: without medicine, they practice embryonic breathing taixi prematurely, forcibly retaining it in the abdomen. Some accumulate cold breath and turn it into illness;

s: Ge Hong, Baopuzi: Inner Chapters (1778), on embryonic breathing: Baopuzi: return the essence, practise embryonic breathing, prolong life.

src.l: Ge Hong, 1778, Baopuzi: Inner Chapters
src.q: live out your years alongside Heaven itself. Return the essence and practice embryonic breathing; prolong life without end." These are all essential sayings of the utmost Dao.
src.qo: 還精胎息延壽無極此皆至道要言也

s: 葛洪 Ge Hong (284–363), Biographies of Divine Immortals, vol.2 (332), on grain avoidance: Biographies of Divine Immortals: he practised abstaining from grains to preserve his life.

src.l: 葛洪 Ge Hong (284–363), 332, Biographies of Divine Immortals, vol.2
src.q: In his youth he loved the Dao, entering Mount Tai to gather herbs and cultivate the arts of juegu [abstaining from grain], retreating from worldly affairs, and preserving his bodily integrity.

s: 李時珍, Compendium of Materia Medica, Volume 10 (1596), on grain avoidance: Bencao citing Baopuzi: a powder recipe for grain avoidance.

src.l: 李時珍, 1596, Compendium of Materia Medica, Volume 10
src.q: The Baopuzi states: The Daoist Dong Wei of Luoyang had a method for grain avoidance 辟穀 [bìgǔ, abstaining from cereals for longevity]. It used about ten ingredients of the class of saposhnikovia seeds 防風子 [seeds of Saposhnikovia divaricata] and licorice, prepared as a powder.
src.qo: 抱朴子云洛陽道士董威辟穀方用防風子甘草 之屬十許種為散

s: 周守忠 Zhou Shouzhong, Classified Compendium on Nurturing Life, vol.4 (1250), on grain avoidance: pine resin as the premier remedy for abstaining from grains.

src.l: 周守忠 Zhou Shouzhong, 1250, Classified Compendium on Nurturing Life, vol.4
src.q: Same source as above Refining pine resin may be undertaken in spring and summer, but never in autumn or winter. It is the premier remedy for abstaining from grains and treating leprosy. If you wish to eat normal food again, simply cease taking it.
src.qo: 同上

s: Various Taoist Masters, Essence of the Taoist Canon (1922), on grain avoidance: one must first abstain from grains before refining energy.

src.l: Various Taoist Masters, 1922, Essence of the Taoist Canon
src.q: According to the inscriptions on refining energy: those who wish to learn this art must first Abstain from Grains Bigu (絕粒/辟穀). A Daoist fasting practice where one stops eating common grains to clear the body of "turbid" energy and rely on "refined" energy.

s: Yi, Chon-jung, 1703-1761, Chʻŏgam yugo (1864), on external alchemy: A Korean scholar declines external alchemy (lead and mercury) for preserving his own essence.

src.l: Yi, Chon-jung, 1703-1761, 1864, Chʻŏgam yugo
src.q: By preserving and being frugal with my essence, my spirit remains abundant. I do not wait for the transformation of lead and mercury [external alchemy]. I have already forgotten the constraints of my physical form.
src.qo: 保嗇神有餘。不待鉉汞化。已忘形迹拘。

s: 高濂, 遵生八牋·卷九 (vol 7) (1596), on inner alchemy: once the mysterious embryo forms it is the neidan, the way of immortality.

src.l: 高濂, 1596, 遵生八牋·卷九 (vol 7)
src.q: Once the mysterious embryo has formed, it spontaneously generates the body; this is the way of the internal elixir and deathlessness.

s: 王圻, 王思義, Collected Illustrations of the Three Realms, juan 30 (1609), on inner alchemy: vital breath is the inner elixir, the compound the outer elixir.

src.l: 王圻, 王思義, 1609, Collected Illustrations of the Three Realms, juan 30
src.q: Later, he met an extraordinary being who transmitted to him a divine elixir, saying: "Vital breath is the inner elixir [nèidān], while medicinal compound is the outer elixir [wàidān].
src.qo: 後遇異人授以神丹曰氣爲內丹 藥爲外丹

s: 尹真人 Yin Zhenren (attrib.), 性命雙修萬神圭旨 :4卷. [China] : 吳之鶴, 明萬曆43 [1615]. (1615), on inner alchemy: embryonic breathing is really the inner elixir; cures disease and extends years.

src.l: 尹真人 Yin Zhenren (attrib.), 1615, 性命雙修萬神圭旨 :4卷. [China] : 吳之鶴, 明萬曆43 [1615].
src.q: It is called Embryonic Breathing [Taixi] in name, but in reality it is the Inner Elixir [Neidan]. It does not only cure disease, it certainly extends one's years.
src.qo: 假名胎息。 實曰內丹。非只治病。決定延年。

s: 魏伯陽 Wei Boyang (attrib.); comm. 蔣一彪 Jiang Yibiao, Collected Explanations of the Ancient-Text Cantong qi (1781), on inner alchemy: Cantong qi commentary: the root and mother of the elixir.

src.l: 魏伯陽 Wei Boyang (attrib.); comm. 蔣一彪 Jiang Yibiao, 1781, Collected Explanations of the Ancient-Text Cantong qi
src.q: When beginning the cultivation of the elixir, one takes the root of Heaven and Earth as the root of the medicine, and takes the mother of yin [receptive cosmic force] and yang [active cosmic force] as the mother of the elixir.

s: Charaka; Avinash Chandra Kaviratna (trans.), Charaka-Samhita (1890), on vigour: Charaka: a preparation restores an old man to the vigour of youth.

src.l: Charaka; Avinash Chandra Kaviratna (trans.), 1890, Charaka-Samhita
src.q: If this preparation is drunk by an old man of even seventy years of age, he gets a large progeny, and enjoys the pleasure of sexual congress like a young man in full vigour of health.

s: Unknown (attrib. Yogisvara), Ramayana Kakawin, Vol. 2 (900), on vigour: Ramayana: bodies regained vigour and vitality.

src.l: Unknown (attrib. Yogisvara), 900, Ramayana Kakawin, Vol. 2
src.q: He embraced the feet of the two princes and wiped them to purity, and their bodies regained their vigour and vitality and were not painful anymore.

s: Samuel Auguste Tissot, Onanism: or, a Treatise upon the Disorders Produced by Masturbation (1766), on vigour: 1766 claim that a bodily liquor circulates fresh vigour.

src.l: Samuel Auguste Tissot, 1766, Onanism: or, a Treatise upon the Disorders Produced by Masturbation
src.q: ’ He afterwards proves by several examples, that a small cause often produces great effects, and finally concludes, ‘is it then surprising that the testicles should furnish a liquor proper to circulate fresh vigour all over the body?

s: Theron Q. Dumont (William Walker Atkinson), The Art and Science of Personal Magnetism (1913), on vigour: felt sense of vigor as the sign of progress.

src.l: Theron Q. Dumont (William Walker Atkinson), 1913, The Art and Science of Personal Magnetism
src.q: You will know when you are on the right track, and will be aware of your progress, by reason of your increasing sense of vigor, vitality and vim.

s: Marsilio Ficino, Three Books on Life; Apology; On the Necessity of Security for Life (1489), on rejuvenation: Ficino: Medea and the Magi restored youth with herbs, rather preserving than restoring.

src.l: Marsilio Ficino, 1489, Three Books on Life; Apology; On the Necessity of Security for Life
src.q: Hence, they say that Medea and the Magi [wise men/magicians] were accustomed to restoring youth with certain herbs, which they do not so much restore as preserve, in the manner of myrobalani [myrobalan, a fruit used in medicine].

s: Crollius, Oswaldus, The Royal Chemistry (1624), on rejuvenation: Croll: the spiritual medicine gives renewal of youth already lost.

src.l: Crollius, Oswaldus, 1624, The Royal Chemistry
src.q: Therefore, in this quintessence or spiritual medicine—which is of a celestial nature and heat, and not of our mortal and corruptible nature—one can find the true fountain of Medicine, the preservation of life, the restoration of health, along with the renewal of youth already lost.
src.qo: Doncques en cette quint'eſſence ou Medecine ſpirituelle, laquelle eſt de la nature & chaleur celeſte, & non en la noſtre mortelle & corruptible, on peut trouuer la vraye fontaine de Medecine, la conſeruation de la vie, la reſtitution de la ſanté, auec la reno- uation de la ieuneſſe ia perduë:

s: Anonymous (Mesopotamian), An Old Babylonian Version of the Gilgamesh Epic (1920), on rejuvenation: Gilgamesh's plant that restores youth to old age.

src.l: Anonymous (Mesopotamian), 1920, An Old Babylonian Version of the Gilgamesh Epic
src.q: Gilgamesh Epic.123 In the Epic the story leads to another episode attached to Gilgamesh, namely, the search for a magic plant growing in deep water, which has the power of restoring old age to youth.

s: [Reusner, Hieronymus], Pandora, that is the noblest gift of God or the worthy and wholesome Philosopher's Stone (1582), on rejuvenation: Pandora: celestial nature found for preservation of life and renewal of youth.

src.l: [Reusner, Hieronymus], 1582, Pandora, that is the noblest gift of God or the worthy and wholesome Philosopher's Stone
src.q: I tell you in truth: the form, state, and essence of the Heaven of Heavens and of the Heavenly Sun is possible to find within mortal or deadly nature, for the preservation of life, and for the replacement and restoration of what is lost, and for the renewal of youth;
src.qo: me des Himels/ vnnd vnsere Sonn be- zieret sie/ wie die Son Gottes den Him- mel bezieret/ vnd dise zwey zusamen ge- thon einfliessend in vns. Ich sag dir in der warheit die gestalt/ stand vñ wäsen

s: Bai Yuchan (白玉蟾, 1194–?), Collected Works of Bai Yuchan (1594), on long life: Guangchengzi: do not exhaust the body or shake the essence and you attain long life.

src.l: Bai Yuchan (白玉蟾, 1194–?), 1594, Collected Works of Bai Yuchan
src.q: Preface to the Collected Works of the Perfected Man Bai Qiongzhan Guangchengzi said to the Yellow Emperor: "Do not exhaust your body, do not shake your essence, and you can attain longevity.

s: Anonymous, Göttingen Notices of Scholarly Matters (1754), on long life: Longaevitas as the third stage of life; hardly twenty in a thousand Europeans reach 80.

src.l: Anonymous, 1754, Göttingen Notices of Scholarly Matters
src.q: What is beyond that and makes up the third stage, to which no certain limits are set, he covers with the word Longaevitas [longevity]. He explains himself regarding this in the preface, and notes the following two points: firstly, that among a thousand Europeans there are hardly twenty who reach the 80th year;

s: J. J. M. de Groot, The Religious System of China, Vol. 4: The Soul in Philosophy and Folk-Conception (1901), on long life: the legend of the Queen Mother's peaches that confer longevity.

src.l: J. J. M. de Groot, 1901, The Religious System of China, Vol. 4: The Soul in Philosophy and Folk-Conception
src.q: PEACHES CONFER LONGEVITY. “ Heaven having eaten his, put away the stones, saying he intended “ to sow them. But Wang-mu said: ‘Those peach trees bear fruit “ only once in three thousand years;

s: 張玉書, 御定佩文韻府·卷二十二之五 (vol 394) (1684), on long life: the star that presides over longevity.

src.l: 張玉書, 1684, 御定佩文韻府·卷二十二之五 (vol 394)
src.q: The star is located within the Zhen [Chariot] constellation and presides over longevity; if it is bright, it signifies long life and flourishing descendants.
src.qo: 星在軫中主壽命明則主壽長子孫昌

s: Ge Hong, Baopuzi: Inner Chapters (1778), on transcendence (xian): Baopuzi: transcendents are rare because they do not die.

src.l: Ge Hong, 1778, Baopuzi: Inner Chapters
src.q: Why then find it strange that transcendent immortals xian [immortals or transcendents] are unique, simply because they do not die alongside ordinary mortals?
src.qo: 何獨怪仙者之異不與凡人皆死乎

s: 張玉書, 御定佩文韻府·卷十六之六 (vol 362) (1684), on transcendence (xian): the First Emperor seeking immortals at the sea.

src.l: 張玉書, 1684, 御定佩文韻府·卷十六之六 (vol 362)
src.q: Seek Immortality Qiu Xian Records of the Grand Historian: Treatise on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices: The First Emperor of Qin traveled east to the sea, performing rituals at famous mountains, great rivers, and to the Eight Spirits to seek immortals like Xianmen and his kind.

s: 高濂, 遵生八牋·卷十七 (vol 14) (1596), on transcendence (xian): a technique of the transcendents that returns one to youth.

src.l: 高濂, 1596, 遵生八牋·卷十七 (vol 14)
src.q: Take for one to two years, and you will return from old age to youth, your facial appearance becoming like a lotus flower, and all illnesses will be eliminated. This is fundamentally the method of the immortals. Believe in it, believe in it!

s: Anonymous, The Golden Art, Called Chemistry (1572), on regeneration: from corruption comes life and regeneratio (alchemical).

src.l: Anonymous, 1572, The Golden Art, Called Chemistry
src.q: For from where corruption happens, thence happens life and regeneratio [regeneration]: because from where death arose, thence would life rise again, and death shall have no more dominion over it.
src.qo: Nam unde fit corruptio, inde fit vita & regeneratio: quia unde mors oriebatur, inde vita resurgeret, & mors ei ultra non dominabitur.

s: Walter Scott, The Hermetic Writings, Volume 1 (1926), on regeneration: Hermetic regeneration of the world.

src.l: Walter Scott, 1926, The Hermetic Writings, Volume 1
src.q: " The Greek must have been either "regeneration" or "new birth." The writer assumes the term "the regeneration of the world" to be already familiar to his readers, and applies it to the restoration which is to follow on the ruin caused by the impiety of the Christians.
src.qo: The Greek must have been either παλιγγενεσία or ἀναγέννησις. The writer assumes the term ἡ τοῦ κόσμου παλιγγενεσία to be already familiar to his readers, (cf. 'haec et talis senectus veniet mundi' above), and applies it to the restoration which is to follow on the ruin caused by the impiety of the Christians.

s: Spener, Philipp Jacob, Die lautere Milch des Evangelii (1712), on regeneration: 1712: a new nature created in a person through Wiedergeburt.

src.l: Spener, Philipp Jacob, 1712, Die lautere Milch des Evangelii
src.q: Just as initially such a new nature is created or worked in a person through wiedergeburt [regeneration/new birth], so must the same always increase and grow, so that the Göttliche bild [Divine image], which was begun there, might be put on more fully and gloriously as time goes on.
src.qo: neue art in dem menschen durch die wieder

s: Unknown, Short Questions (1784), on regeneration: 1550 catechism: grace offers the new birth, faith grasps it.

src.l: Unknown, 1784, Short Questions
src.q: Of the New Birth. It cannot happen any other way: Grace offers it, Christ has earned it, and faith grasps it and carries it home. The Word proclaims it and the Holy Spirit confirms it.
src.qo: Von der Wiedergeburt. Anders kan es nicht geschehen: Die Gnade reichets dar, Christus hats erworben, und der Glaube ergreiffets und tragts heim. Das Wort verkündiget und der Heilige Geist beståtigt solches.

s: John Climacus, The Ladder of Divine Ascent (1633), on acedia: Climacus: acedia brings a general death to the monk.

src.l: John Climacus, 1633, The Ladder of Divine Ascent
src.q: Other vices are each destroyed by a single virtue, but acedia brings a general death to the monk. A courageous soul brings a dead mind back to life, but acedia and laziness scatter all wealth.

s: Thomas Aquinas, Summary of Theology: Second Part of the Second Part (1491), on acedia: Aquinas: acedia is sadness regarding a spiritual good.

src.l: Thomas Aquinas, 1491, Summary of Theology: Second Part of the Second Part
src.q: Question acedia [spiritual sloth] from other vices, and it is a special vice. I answer that it must be said that acedia is sadness regarding a spiritual good;
src.qo: Questio acidia ab aliis viciis. et est speciale vicium. Respondeo dicendum quod acidia sit tristitia de spirituali bono:

s: Evelyn Underhill, Evelyn Underhill The Mystic Way (1913), on acedia: manual work as the hermit's protection against accidie, the boredom of prayer.

src.l: Evelyn Underhill, 1913, Evelyn Underhill The Mystic Way
src.q: Such manual work was the great protection of the hermit against the monastic sin of "accidie"; the restless misery and boredom which comes over the contemplative when his spiritual insight fails him,

s: Angelo Poliziano, First Century of Miscellanies (1489), on automaton: Poliziano: automata were machines that seemed to act of their own accord.

src.l: Angelo Poliziano, 1489, First Century of Miscellanies
src.q: It appears, therefore, that they were commonly called Automata: which mechanics constructed in such a way that they seemed to perform some action of their own accord, as if by an unknown cause.
src.qo: Apparet ergo Automata appellari solita: quae ita mechanici fabricabantur: ut sua sponte efficere quippiam: uelut ignara causa uiderentur.

s: Peucer, Kaspar, Commentarius de praecipuis generibus divinationum, in quo a prophetiis autoritate divina traditis & a physicis coniecturis, discernuntur artes et imposturae diabolicae, atque observationes natae ex superstitione et cum hac coniunctae ... (1560), on automaton: Peucer: art builds automata of iron wheels and weights that imitate the heavens.

src.l: Peucer, Kaspar, 1560, Commentarius de praecipuis generibus divinationum, in quo a prophetiis autoritate divina traditis & a physicis coniecturis, discernuntur artes et imposturae diabolicae, atque observationes natae ex superstitione et cum hac coniunctae ...
src.q: Art constructs αὐτόματα [automata/self-moving machines], by which it imitates the rotations and revolutions of the world with iron wheels and cogwheels, arranged and joined in a certain order, and with a weight attached by which they are pushed and pulled and turned around;
src.qo: Construit ars αὐτόματα, quibus effingit mundi circumactus & conuersiones rotulis ferreis, & dentatis, certo dispositis & coagmentatis ordine,

s: Hero of Alexandria; Wilhelm Schmidt (ed.), Complete Extant Works of Hero of Alexandria, Vol. 1 (1899), on automaton: Hero's automaton theatres and why they were popular.

src.l: Hero of Alexandria; Wilhelm Schmidt (ed.), 1899, Complete Extant Works of Hero of Alexandria, Vol. 1
src.q: THE AUTOMATON THEATERS OF HERO OF ALEXANDRIA. The two types of automata. I The display of automata (automaton theater) enjoyed great popularity among the ancients, first because a manifold skill is developed in it, and second because the spectacle (presented) is simply astonishing.

s: A gloss in the 1546 Compendium de anima ranks the soul's power in three orders from most common to least: the motive, by which the plant-like or vegetative power is found; the apprehensive, by which the animal or sensitive soul is known; and the rational, by which the intellectual soul is known.

src.l: Avicenna (Ibn Sina), Andrea Alpago (trans.), 1546, Compendium de anima
src.q: In the third order, however, is the rational power, which is less common than both the motive and apprehensive powers; through this ranking, the power of the intellectual soul is known and discovered.
src.qo: In tertio uero ordine est uirtus rationalis, quæ est minus cõmunis, quàm motiua, & quàm apprehensiua

src.l: Avicenna (Ibn Sina), Andrea Alpago (trans.), 1546, Compendium de anima
src.q: In tertio uero ordine est uirtus rationalis, quæ est minus cõmunis, quàm motiua, & quàm apprehensiua

s: Plato (Republic III, 386d–387a) quotes Iliad 16.856–57 among the lines to be struck from poetry: at Patroclus's death the psychē flies from his limbs and goes to Hades, lamenting, leaving its manhood and youth behind; the psychē is what leaves the body at death, not what animates thought.

src.l: Plato, 1894, The Republic (Greek text)
src.q: and the soul, flying from the limbs, went down to Hades, > bewailing its fate, leaving behind its manliness and youth;
src.qo: ψυχὴ δ᾽ ἐκ ῥεθέων πταμένη Ἄϊδόσδε βεβήκει, > ὃν πότμον γοόωσα, λιποῦσ᾽ ἀνδροτῆτα καὶ ἥβην

s: Plutarch (Non posse suaviter vivi secundum Epicurum 26–27) quotes Iliad 9.408–9: a man's psychē cannot come back, cannot be plundered or caught, once it has passed the barrier of the teeth; the psychē leaves by the mouth.

src.loc: Non posse suaviter vivi 26 (Moralia 1104–5), quoting Il. 9.408–9; scan 427

s: The Life of Homer printed with the 1524 Aldine Iliad credits Homer with first announcing the soul's immortality, citing the line where the psychē flies from the limbs to Hades, and glosses Hades as the unseen place, 'whether one should call it the air or an underground place'.

src.l: Homer, Pseudo-Plutarch, 1524, Omerou ilias = Homeri Ilias (Venice: Aldus and Andrea Asolano), with the pseudo-Plutarchan Life of Homer
src.loc: Life of Homer, on the soul; scan 72
src.q: τίς οὖν τοῦτο πρῶτον ἀνεφώνησεν; Ὅμηρος εἰπὼν ἀλλαχόθι καὶ ταῦτα. ψυχὴ δ' ἐκ ῥεθέων πταμένη, Ἀϊδόσδε βεβήκει, εἰς τὸν ἀειδῆ καὶ ἀόρατον· εἴτε ἀέρα θείη τις, εἴτε ὑπόγειον τόπον.

src.l: Homer, Pseudo-Plutarch, 1524, Omerou ilias = Homeri Ilias (Venice: Aldus and Andrea Asolano), with the pseudo-Plutarchan Life of Homer
src.q: into the unseen and invisible place, whether one should call it the air or an underground place.
